selection_rate.description: Fraction of population selected as parents each generation.

elitism_rate.description: Fraction of the population carried over verbatim each generation, bypassing crossover, mutation, and filters. Must be less than selection_rate.

selection_scheme.description: Selection scheme: 'nsga2' (default) ranks by Pareto non-domination and crowding distance over the individual fitness components; 'nsga2-replicate' ranks identically but deduplicates the (mu + lambda) pool before sorting and replicates the distinct survivors back up to population_size, apportioning copies by 1 / (1 + rank); 'weighted' ranks by the weighted-average fitness scalar, but converges prematurely and is retained for comparison.

p_trigger.description: Per-requirement probability of mutating the trigger.

p_response.description: Per-requirement probability of mutating the response.

p_timing.description: Per-requirement probability of mutating the timing.

p_add_assumption.description: Both modes: probability a mutation appends a new environment assumption (fairness over an input) instead of rewriting an existing requirement/formula.

p_conditional_assumption.description: Of the appended assumptions, the fraction guarded by a random input atom rather than by 'true'.

strengthen_assumptions.description: Mutate assumption timings in the strengthening direction rather than the weakening one. Retained so the two directions can be compared.

allow_output_assumptions.description: Allow freshly added environment assumptions to reference output atoms as well as inputs. False (the default) keeps them input-only and so well-separated by construction.

p_assumption.description: Probability of mutating an assumption-side section (INITIALLY/REQUIRE/ASSUME).

p_guarantee.description: Probability of mutating a guarantee-side section (PRESET/ASSERT/GUARANTEE).

p_temporal.description: Probability that a chosen section formula is rewritten by the temporal-structure mutation (may insert/drop/swap X/F/G/U/R/W) rather than the skeleton-preserving propositional rewrite.

repair_mode.description: Repair strategy: 'monolithic' (default) evolves the whole specification at once; 'muc' extracts a minimal unrealizable core, evolves only that sub-specification, reintegrates it with the untouched non-core guarantees, and repeats.

muc_max_iterations.description: muc mode only: cap on the outer extract-repair-reintegrate loop.

default_bound.description: Trace-length bound k for bounded model counting.

metric.description: How trace counts become a similarity score: 'direct' takes the ratio of counts (a true overlap, but bound-dependent); 'logarithmic' (default) takes the ratio of their logarithms, comparing growth rates and staying stable as the bound grows.

run_vacuity.description: Drop candidates whose assumptions are jointly unsatisfiable, which are realizable for free.

run_well_separation.description: Drop candidates that are not well-separated: ones the system can satisfy vacuously by forcing its own assumptions to fail. Strictly stronger than run_vacuity, but each test is a full ltlsynt query, so it is off by default.

intervals.description: How often each per-generation filter runs, in generations (1 = every generation). The final generation always runs every filter.

black_timeout_ms.description: Timeout per black SAT query in milliseconds.

ltlsynt_timeout_ms.description: Per-call ltlsynt realizability timeout in milliseconds. 0 (default) is no timeout; a call exceeding it is killed and treated as unrealizable.

ltl2tgba_timeout_ms.description: Per-call ltl2tgba automaton-construction timeout in milliseconds. 0 (default) is no timeout.

parallel.description: Thread pool size. Omit to use hardware concurrency.

max_concurrent_realizability.description: Cap on ltlsynt processes running at once, independent of the thread pool. 0 (default) is unlimited; a positive value bounds peak RAM.

ltlfilt_batchers.description: How many ltlfilt batches may run at once. Coalescing concurrent simplify calls trades latency for CPU; 4 (default) suits campaigns, higher approaches baseline wall time, 0 disables batching.

simplify_engine.description: Where LTL simplification runs. libspot (default) calls the linked library in process; ltlfilt spawns the command-line tool. Output is identical either way, but an exec costs ~8ms of startup against ~0.02ms of simplification, and ltlfilt_batchers applies only under ltlfilt.

report_cpu_timing.description: Print the CPU-attribution report (your code vs. external CLI tools).

max_scoring_failure_rate.description: Fraction of a generation whose fitness scoring may throw before the run aborts. A single failure per generation is always tolerated.

dashboard.description: Stream progress to <output-dir>/progress.jsonl and copy the live dashboard page beside it. Off by default; --dashboard also enables it.
